rows.note: This is the all-purpose adjective for someone who is older, especially in a relatively formal description.

example.english: Senior people should sit in front.
example.jyutping: nin4 zoeng2 jan4 si6 jiu3 co5 cin4 min6

rows.note: Use this for a person, post, or role that is higher in rank or status than another.

example.english: They are a senior manager at the company and do not need to seek approval at every level.
example.traditional: 佢係公司高級主管，唔使逐級請示。
example.jyutping: keoi5 hai6 gung1 si1 gou1 kap1 zyu2 gun2 m4 sai2 zuk6 kap1 cing2 si6

rows.traditional: 大 A N 年嘅人
rows.jyutping: daai6 A N nin4 ge3 jan4
rows.note: Use this noun phrase for someone who is N years older than A, such as “someone four years older than me.”

example.english: They are my senior by four years.
example.jyutping: keoi5 hai6 daai6 ngo5 sei3 nin4 ge3 jan4

rows.note: Use this polite everyday term when “senior” means an elderly person.

example.english: The senior is crossing the road, so let’s wait.
example.traditional: 老人家過馬路，我哋等吓啦。
example.jyutping: lou5 jan4 gaa1 gwo3 maa5 lou6 ngo5 dei6 dang2 haa5 laa1

rows.note: Use this in an educational context for a student in the final graduating year.

example.english: My cousin is a senior student and has to take the public exam this year.
example.traditional: 我表弟係畢業班學生，今年要考公開試。
example.jyutping: ngo5 biu2 dai6 hai6 bat1 jip6 baan1 hok6 saang1 gam1 nin4 jiu3 haau2 gung1 hoi1 si3

rows.jyutping: duk6 gan2 zeoi3 hau6 jat1 nin4 ge3 A
rows.note: Use this attributive construction for a student who is currently in their final academic year.
Use this for a higher-ranking person in a workplace or chain of command, rather than merely an older person.

example.english: My senior told me to come in earlier tomorrow.
example.traditional: 我上司叫我聽日返早啲。
example.jyutping: ngo5 soeng6 si1 giu3 ngo5 teng1 jat6 faan1 zou2 di1
